summary: Iteration 12 verifies the user story 'bildstöd ska komma med när man gör om materialet'. All 6 tests in /app/backend/tests/test_bildstod.py pass (2 unit + 4 real-AI/integration). UNIT MergeFigures.test_01 — ai.merge_figures('Ett äpple är rött.\nEn banan är gul.', [], [n=1 near_text='Ett äpple', n=2 near_text='']) returned markdown with '[[FIGURE:1]]' appended INLINE on the first line (right after 'Ett äpple är rött.') and '[[FIGURE:2]]' appended at the very end (empty near_text => tail), out_figs length 2 — matches spec exactly. UNIT MergeFigures.test_02 — detection box [0,0,100,100] overlapping an existing OCR fig box [0,0,100,100] (IoU=1.0 > 0.3) was correctly skipped; non-overlapping [500,500,700,700] was added with n=2 (continues from max OCR n=1), resulting in exactly one new placeholder in markdown. REAL AI (2 paid Gemini-fast calls total — within budget of 3): synthetic Swedish school page (1240x1754 white JPEG) with four word lines each followed by a small distinct coloured pictogram (red circle 'äpple', yellow crescent 'banan', green tree 'träd', blue house 'hus') + a larger yellow sun illustration -> page.status='done', len(figures)>=4 (actually seen 4-6 depending on model run — assertion passed), EVERY figure had an https CommHub url + file_id, every figure box_2d area < 50% of page (no whole-page swallowing — pipeline.drop_whole_page + grow_box 'neutral never grows' intact for the white page), and [[FIGURE:n]] placeholders present in the OCR markdown. POST /api/process with instruction 'Skriv om texten enklare' (1 paid Gemini-balanced call via run_instruction + INSTRUCTION_SYSTEM) produced generated-doc markdown containing >=3 '![...](fig:HEX)' refs (bildstöd kept inline next to the corresponding text), generated-doc ZIP contained >=3 bilder/*.jpg files, and docx export (format=docx) returned 200 with valid PK zip magic. Settings pinned speed_mode=fast + primary_provider=gemini pre- and post-test. Frontend smoke on 390x844 (mobile) + 1366x860 (desktop): CopyThat login screen 'AI-läsning av kurs- och studiematerial' renders clean on both, no red-screen, no pageerror; only 401s on /api/me pre-login (expected). MarkdownView inline-pictogram regex (frontend/src/components/MarkdownView.tsx:13) splits on both '[[FIGURE:\d+]]' and '![cap](fig:HEX)' and renders an Image when the figure map resolves — so raw placeholder text never leaks when figures are supplied. Seed data (TEST_BILDSTOD_Course + TEST_BILDSTOD_Doc + 1 page + its figures + generated doc) cleaned up at module teardown and verified: 0 TEST_ courses, 0 TEST_ docs remaining; owner (emil@jawel.se) 8 docs untouched. Total paid AI calls: 2 (1 OCR + 1 /process).
critical_code_review_comments: ai.merge_figures() uses lines[idx] = lines[idx] + f' [[FIGURE:{n}]]' which places the placeholder ON the same line as the near_text match — perfect for inline bildstöd right after the word; MarkdownView's Inline() splits the paragraph string on '[[FIGURE:\d+]]' and renders a 40x40 Image, so the pictogram appears inline directly after the word in the preview. End-to-end alignment is correct.

ai.merge_figures() anchor matching uses case-insensitive substring of the first 40 chars of near_text (anchor = near_text.strip().lower()[:40]). Robust against capitalisation and leading punctuation. If near_text is longer than 40 chars (unlikely given the prompt asks for 'exact word or first words'), only the first 40 chars are used — still a correct and useful match. No regression risk observed.

pipeline.FIGURE_PROMPT (ai.py:294-302) and OCR_PROMPT both now state 'EACH separate object gets its own box — a row of pictograms = one box per pictogram' and 'logo+shape+words = ONE box'; detect_figures ALWAYS runs after the OCR pass and merge_figures adds any extras not already placed. This is the right layered design: the OCR pass picks the obvious ones and anchors them in text, the dedicated pass picks up small bildstöd next to words that the OCR pass skipped.
pipeline._crop_box() minimum area is 0.0005 * w * h (0.05% of page) — a 60x60 pictogram on a 1240x1754 page is 3600px² vs threshold 1086px², so pictograms survive. Good.

pipeline.refine_figures() + grow_box() 'neutral never grows' guard (max-min < 60) correctly left the small coloured pictograms sitting on WHITE background untouched during this iteration (previously it already protected cream carton against the Arla badge case). Verified in test_02 by every figure area < 50% of the page.

ai.INSTRUCTION_SYSTEM now says 'PICTURE SUPPORT (bildstöd) IS ESSENTIAL ... include that exact image reference (![caption](fig:ID)) next to the corresponding text — small pictograms directly after the word they support, larger images on their own line.' End-to-end test confirms Gemini-balanced respects this: generated doc kept >=3 image refs when the OCR input had bildstöd references.

MarkdownView.tsx line 19 regex matches EXACTLY '^![cap](fig:HEX)$' at block level and inline via the same pattern — the id capture group index differs between the two matches (block fig[1] vs fig[2]). Line 40 handles it via 'fig[2] ?? \`n${fig[1]}\`' — correct, but if a future refactor changes the regex order this will silently misroute lookups. Minor fragility, not a bug today.

export.page_markdown_with_refs() + document_markdown() correctly transform [[FIGURE:n]] -> ![caption](fig:ID) at ZIP/docx time, keeping the inline placement; frontend MarkdownView reads the same ![cap](fig:ID) pattern inside the Inline() splitter, so the generated-doc preview also renders pictograms inline. Verified via test_03 ZIP export containing images.

No ObjectId leak (all mongo queries use projection {_id:0}); no sync blocking (crop_and_store/refine_figures use asyncio.to_thread); env vars only, no hard-coded URLs. No code smells to flag this round.
